Kidzoi Enables Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory Activity and Variant Effect Prediction in Kidney.

Kidzoi is a kidney cell-type-specific sequence-to-function deep learning model created by transfer learning from the pretrained Borzoi model using single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data. It enables prediction of regulatory activity and variant effects in a cell-type-specific manner within the kidney, addressing the limitation that no single pretrained model covers all cell types and conditions. This approach provides a practical way to adapt existing S2F models to new tissues without training from scratch.

Integration of single-cell and bulk transcriptomics for deciphering prognostic value and immunotherapeutic features of floatptosis-mediated cell death in lung adenocarcinoma.

This study builds a prognostic model for lung adenocarcinoma based on genes linked to floatptosis, a newly described form of vacuolar cell death triggered by outer membrane vesicles from a Bergeyella cardium variant. By combining single-cell and bulk transcriptomics, the authors link floatptosis-related gene expression to patient survival and to features relevant to immunotherapy response. The work is exploratory and the clinical utility of the model remains to be validated.

Multi-omics and pathological landscape of a senescence-associated prognostic model in bladder urothelial carcinoma.

This study identifies cellular senescence-associated gene signatures through pan-cancer screening and builds a prognostic risk model for bladder urothelial carcinoma that integrates multi-omics and pathological data. The model stratifies patients by risk and links senescence signals to tumor microenvironment features, offering a framework for molecular risk stratification in BLCA.

PoolParty: streamlined design of DNA sequence libraries in Python.

PoolParty is a Python package that streamlines the design of DNA sequence libraries for multiplex assays such as MPRA, DMS, and MAVE, as well as for in silico analysis of genomic AI models. It addresses the lack of purpose-built software that makes library design tedious and error-prone, providing a reusable tool for the genomics community.

Assessing the predictive potential of the Holstein bovine sperm methylome for bull fertility using machine learning.

This study tested whether DNA methylation patterns in Holstein bull sperm can predict bull fertility using machine learning models. Using existing methylation data, the authors evaluated the predictive power of sperm methylome features for fertility outcomes. The work assesses the feasibility of developing an operational methylation-based biomarker tool for the dairy cattle industry.

Experimental benchmarking of in silico annotations at prostate cancer risk loci and hypothesis-generating cross-cancer prioritisation of ovarian risk variants.

The authors re-analyzed a massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) covering 208 prostate cancer risk SNPs across three cell lines, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs at FDR < 0.10. They then benchmarked standard in silico annotation tools against these experimental results and used the findings to prioritize ovarian cancer risk variants by cross-cancer transfer. The work provides an experimentally grounded reference for evaluating computational regulatory variant predictions.

Ultra-sensitive Mapping of Cell-free DNA-derived Methylomes Reveals Brain-specific Epigenetic Alterations Implicated in Alzheimer's Disease.

The authors applied LABS, an ultra-sensitive linear amplification-based whole-genome bisulfite sequencing method, to profile methylation in serum cell-free DNA from age- and sex-matched pathologically confirmed Alzheimer's disease cases and non-AD controls. They detected altered methylation features in blood cfDNA, including brain-specific epigenetic signatures, suggesting cfDNA methylomes can capture AD-related changes non-invasively.

Agent_K: An Agent-Orchestrated Pipeline for Mapping Genes to Biosynthetic Pathway towards Metabolite Discovery.

Agent_K is an agent-orchestrated framework that automates the entire workflow from bacterial whole-genome sequence analysis to biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) identification, pathway mapping, and candidate metabolite discovery. It addresses the fragmentation of existing computational tools by integrating data processing, annotation, and analysis across heterogeneous platforms with minimal manual intervention. This enables more streamlined genome-guided natural product discovery.

Reference-free isoform discovery links unannotated RNA processing to disease risk.

The authors present Torino, a computational framework that discovers RNA processing patterns directly from population-scale RNA sequencing data without relying on existing transcript annotations. By adapting non-negative matrix factorization to model how read coverage varies across samples, Torino identifies unannotated RNA processing events and links them to disease risk across tissues, individuals, and disease states.

Streamline CNV - A Handy Nextflow Pipeline for Chromosomal Copy Number Variation Analysis.

SLCNV is a user-friendly Nextflow pipeline that streamlines chromosomal copy number variation analysis from low-pass whole genome sequencing data, addressing the need for accessible tools for wet-lab biologists. It automates many copy number-related analyses, reducing the computational expertise required to detect aneuploidy and CNVs in cells and tissues.

Viscous mechanical cues encode metastatic behavior through cytoskeletal-nuclear coupling and chromatin remodeling.

This study shows that the viscosity of a tumor's mechanical environment can mimic the effects of stiffness on cancer cells. Cells grown on soft but viscous substrates develop stiffness-like traits, including increased cell stiffness, nuclear YAP accumulation, and enhanced migration through narrow constrictions. Epigenomic and transcriptomic profiling link these changes to cytoskeletal-nuclear coupling and chromatin remodeling, suggesting viscosity is a distinct mechanical cue driving metastatic behavior.

Combining MAVEs and computational predictors improves variant classification across ancestries in hereditary cancer genes.

This paper shows that widely used computational variant effect predictors carry ancestry-related bias because their training data under-represent global populations, leading to uneven classification of hereditary cancer gene variants across ancestries. The authors demonstrate that combining multiplexed assays of variant effect (MAVEs) with population-free predictors yields classification evidence that generalizes across populations, improving fairness and accuracy in variant interpretation.

Chromatin compartment shifting is recurrent and associated with epigenetic reprogramming in prostate cancer.

By integrating Hi-C, ATAC-seq, and transcriptomic data from 18 clinical prostate samples spanning benign, primary, and castration-resistant cancer, this study maps A/B chromatin compartment changes while correcting for copy number variation and tumor purity. It finds recurrent shifts from inactive (B) to active (A) compartments in prostate tumors that are linked to epigenetic reprogramming, suggesting 3D genome reorganization contributes to prostate carcinogenesis and progression.

Catalytic DNA for Precision Diagnostics: DNAzyme-Based Approaches to Single-Nucleotide Polymorphism Detection.

This review examines DNAzyme-based biosensors for detecting single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), the most common form of human genetic variation and key biomarkers for disease risk and precision medicine. It argues that these catalytic DNA sensors overcome limitations of conventional genotyping methods—such as reliance on sophisticated instruments and poor tolerance of complex sample matrices—by combining programmable nucleic acid recognition with isothermal catalytic signal amplification.

Ultrafast alignment-free detection of viral genome variation with bronko.

The authors present bronko, an alignment-free framework that detects viral genome variation directly from sequencing reads, avoiding the computational cost of traditional alignment-based variant calling. It uses locality-sensitive bucketing to rapidly identify SNPs relative to a reference and a k-mer count pseudo-mapping approach, enabling scaling to massive viral sequencing datasets.

O-acetylation mediates four distinct structural variants of the pneumococcal vaccine serotype 15A capsule polysaccharide.

This study re-examined the capsule polysaccharides of pneumococcal serogroup 15 and found that O-acetylation generates four distinct structural variants of the 15A capsule, not just the previously recognized 15A and 15F forms. The findings show that conventional serological and molecular typing can miss O-acetylation differences that may affect vaccine coverage and serotype classification.

Proteomics-Guided Discovery of Candidate Enzymes for Degradation of a Rare Pyruvylated Glycosaminogalactan by a Newly Isolated Luteolibacter Strain.

The authors isolated a new Luteolibacter strain capable of degrading EPSLp, a high-molecular-mass exopolysaccharide from Lactiplantibacillus pentosus that contains an uncommon pyruvylated GalNAc-Gal motif. Anticancer activity of sodium propionate in hepatocellular carcinoma cells via downregulation of HDAC2 and HDAC6.

This study combines bioinformatics analysis of public HCC transcriptomic datasets with in vitro experiments to show that sodium propionate, a short-chain fatty acid, exerts anticancer effects on hepatocellular carcinoma cells by downregulating the histone deacetylases HDAC2 and HDAC6. The work identifies these HDACs as key epigenetic targets through which sodium propionate may act, suggesting a potential repurposing opportunity for this metabolite in liver cancer.

Conservative evolution of genetic and features in Caenorhabditis becei, an experimentally tractable gonochoristic worm.

The authors identify Caenorhabditis becei as an experimentally tractable gonochoristic (male-female) nematode species, addressing the field's reliance on self-fertile hermaphroditic Elegans Group species. They show that transmission-genetic properties known from androdioecious Elegans Group species are conserved in this Japonica Group species, making it a useful new model for evolutionary genetics and genomics.

CALB1 expression in meningioma: associations with progression-free survival and chromosome arm 6q loss.

This study examined calbindin D28K (CALB1) protein expression in 231 meningioma tissue cores from 147 patients and found associations between CALB1 immunoreactivity, progression-free survival, and chromosome arm 6q loss. Large language and foundation models in predictive plant breeding: Capabilities, evidence, and challenges.

This review examines how large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge graphs, and biological foundation models can support predictive plant breeding by integrating genomic, phenotypic, environmental, and multi-omics data with scientific literature. Molecular mechanisms of colorectal cancer: from carcinogenesis and molecular classification to targeted therapy.

This review synthesizes the molecular mechanisms driving colorectal cancer, from the stepwise accumulation of genetic and epigenetic alterations that transform normal colonic epithelium into malignancy, through molecular classification systems, to the implications for targeted therapy. It emphasizes how interactions among genetic changes, epigenetic modifications, and environmental/lifestyle factors shape prevention, diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment. The work serves as a consolidated reference for understanding the molecular landscape of CRC.

Lysine crotonylation acts as an epigenetic switch for glutamate neurotransmission and spatial memory.

This study identifies histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr) as a key epigenetic regulator of long-term memory consolidation. Spatial learning induces distinct spatiotemporal patterns of Kcr across hippocampal subregions, and Kcr appears to act as a molecular switch controlling glutamatergic neurotransmission and spatial memory. The work extends the known epigenetic repertoire beyond histone acetylation in memory formation.

A recall-rescue fuzzy layer over paired Z-DNA Hunter scans for fast Z-DNA detection.

The authors present Z-DNA-Fuzzy Hunter 1.1.0, a tool that improves detection of Z-DNA-forming regions by combining a permissive scan (broad candidate capture) with a stringent scan (high-confidence support) and integrating them through a fuzzy expert layer. This dual-scan recall-rescue strategy aims to overcome the sensitivity-specificity trade-off in sequence-based Z-DNA prediction while remaining fast and interpretable.

Inferring causal networks for genomic trios with high-dimensional confounding variables.

The paper introduces a new method for inferring causal relationships between molecular phenotypes (like gene expression) using genetic variants as instruments under the Mendelian randomization principle, specifically designed to handle high-dimensional confounding variables such as other genes, processes, and demographics. Existing methods struggle with such high-dimensional confounders, and this work aims to robustly account for them in causal network inference for genomic trio data.

XenoMix: estimating mouse content from DNA methylation data of Patient-Derived Xenograft models.

XenoMix is a lightweight computational tool that estimates the proportion of mouse DNA contamination in DNA methylation microarray data from Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) models. It addresses the common problem of mixed human-mouse signal in PDX epigenomic profiling, enabling researchers to quantify and account for contamination without additional experiments. This improves the reliability of epigenetic analyses in PDX-based cancer studies.

SCCmecExtractor: a tool for extracting staphylococcal cassette chromosome elements from whole-genome sequences.

SCCmecExtractor is a new lightweight Python toolkit that identifies and extracts complete staphylococcal cassette chromosome (SCC) elements from whole-genome assemblies by detecting degenerate attachment site patterns. Unlike existing SCCmec typing tools, it can extract the full element sequence and classify SCC elements even when they lack methicillin resistance genes. This enables more comprehensive analysis of these mobile genetic elements in staphylococci.

The Promise and Limitations of Metabolic Trait Prediction Across Diverse Bacteria.

This study systematically tests whether metabolic traits like substrate utilization can be reliably predicted from bacterial genomes alone. Comparing four common bioinformatic tools against high-throughput growth phenotypes of 186 marine bacteria, the authors find that prediction accuracy is limited and highly variable across taxa and substrates, especially for simple substrates. The results caution against assuming that genome-based metabolic predictions are universally reliable.

Long-read sequencing of FLG identifies extensive copy number variation in exon 3 and detects rare loss-of-function variants.

Long-read technology overcame the limitations of short-read methods in this repetitive region, improving detection of clinically relevant LOF variants.

ogMapper improves speed and memory for short-sequencing read mapping using a novel guided sparse genome index.

ogMapper introduces a novel guided sparse genome indexing strategy for short-read mapping that reduces the memory footprint of the genome index to roughly 0.5 times the genome size (β ≈ 0.5), compared to β ≈ 1.9 for minimap2 and β ≈ 10 for bwa-mem2. This lower memory requirement, combined with improved speed, makes read mapping feasible on less powerful hardware, broadening its applicability in research and clinical settings.
